story.head: Jensen meets his old team
paras: The Senators (9-5-1) beat San Jose 5-1 last night, while the Ducks (5-7-1) lost 7-6 to Buffalo on Thursday. Going in, the Sens are third in the Atlantic (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Ducks sixth in the Pacific (tied for 26th).

The Senators’ record (.633) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.563), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. The Ducks’ record (.423) is about what their chances are worth.

The Senators rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd), play slow, tight games (3rd lowest) and draw more penalties than they take (4th). As for the Ducks, they play some of the league’s fastest games (3rd). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (30th), so the Senators keep dangerous shots away, but them give up a lot of them. Anaheim has allowed 3.85 goals a game, the second most in the league. Both teams like to hit, especially the Ducks (4th), so expect plenty of it.

Tim Stützle (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 15 GP) leads the Senators in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Drake Batherson (9 G / 8 A / 17 P in 15 GP) is next in line, with ten points in his last five games and four goals in six games against Anaheim since 2023-24. For the Ducks, Leo Carlsson (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Beckett Sennecke (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 13 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Jonas Johansson (1-1-0 / .859 SV% in 3 GS) is expected to start for Ottawa, and Laurent Brossoit for Anaheim, his first start of the season.
The Senators usually control more of the chances than the Ducks do.
